questions.stem: An HTTPS request targets the FortiGate interface address itself. Which policy plane first?

options.text: Local-in policy and interface service access
options.feedback: Correct. The destination is the FortiGate itself, so local-in handling and interface service settings govern it.

options.text: Forward firewall policy and security profiles
options.feedback: Not correct: Forward policies apply to transit traffic, not a packet terminating on the FortiGate.

options.text: SD-WAN service rule and application signature
options.feedback: Not correct: SD-WAN steering concerns egress selection, not local service admission.

options.text: Central SNAT rule and return-path session
options.feedback: Not correct: SNAT is not the first control for a request addressed to the firewall.

questions.stem: Which configuration table controls inbound local-in policy for IPv6?

options.text: config firewall policy6
options.feedback: Not correct: A forward policy table is not the local-in table.

options.text: config firewall local-in-policy6
options.feedback: Correct. FortiOS separates IPv6 local-in rules into local-in-policy6.

options.text: config system interface6
options.feedback: Not correct: Interface addressing does not define ordered local-in service rules.

options.text: config router access-list6
options.feedback: Not correct: A router access list is not the FortiGate local-in policy object.

questions.stem: Per-policy local-in logs are missing though global logging is enabled. What next?

options.text: The destination's DNS cache timeout
options.feedback: Not correct: DNS cache state does not enable a local-in rule's log option.

options.text: The FortiAP radio's LLDP setting
options.feedback: Not correct: AP LLDP affects wireless neighbor behavior, not local-in logging.

options.text: The matching rule's logtraffic setting
options.feedback: Correct. Global local-in logging and the rule logtraffic setting work together.

options.text: The transit policy's application-control profile
options.feedback: Not correct: A transit profile does not enable per-rule local-in logs.

questions.stem: Allow HTTPS from an admin subnet and deny it from others. What design fits?

options.text: A broad accept rule for every source
options.feedback: Not correct: A broad accept exposes the service beyond the admin subnet.

options.text: Only disable HTTPS in interface settings
options.feedback: Not correct: Disabling HTTPS blocks authorized and unauthorized administrators.

options.text: Rely on a forward-policy implicit deny
options.feedback: Not correct: Forward-policy defaults do not replace local-in policy design.

options.text: Ordered source-specific allow followed by deny
options.feedback: Correct. Explicit ordered local-in rules express the intended source boundary.

questions.stem: Which template runs once on a model device during Add Device?

options.text: Pre-Run CLI Template assigned to a model
options.feedback: Correct. Pre-run templates bootstrap model-device configuration and are unassigned after success.

options.text: Post-VDOM Copy template on every device
options.feedback: Not correct: Post-VDOM Copy is a normal install phase, not one-time model bootstrap.

options.text: A policy package installed before discovery
options.feedback: Not correct: A policy package is not the pre-run template lifecycle.

options.text: A device revision retrieved from FortiGate
options.feedback: Not correct: Revision retrieval is a separate configuration-management operation.

questions.stem: A command must exist before the policy package installs. Which position fits?

options.text: Post-VDOM Copy after package installation
options.feedback: Not correct: Post-VDOM Copy runs after the package.

options.text: Pre-VDOM Copy during installation
options.feedback: Correct. Pre-VDOM Copy runs before the package during installation.

options.text: A scheduled script after later revision retrieval
options.feedback: Not correct: A later script does not guarantee required install ordering.

options.text: A one-time pre-run template on every device
options.feedback: Not correct: Pre-run templates are restricted to model devices.

questions.stem: What is the default position for a regular CLI template?

options.text: Pre-run before Add Device starts
options.feedback: Not correct: Pre-run belongs to model bootstrap.

options.text: Pre-VDOM Copy before the package
options.feedback: Not correct: Pre-VDOM Copy is selectable but not the default.

options.text: Post-VDOM Copy after the policy package
options.feedback: Correct. Post-VDOM Copy is the default for regular templates.

options.text: Only after manual revision retrieval
options.feedback: Not correct: Revision retrieval is a different workflow.

questions.stem: A pre-run template failed on the Device Database. What is the retry path?

options.text: Wait for it to self-assign again
options.feedback: Not correct: A failed pre-run template is not guaranteed to self-assign again.

options.text: Move it into a firewall policy package only
options.feedback: Not correct: A CLI template is not replaced by a policy package.

options.text: Delete the model device and skip verification
options.feedback: Not correct: Deleting the device discards state and avoids diagnosis.

options.text: Correct it, reassign it, then run install
options.feedback: Correct. The guide calls for review/update, manual reassignment, and an install retry.

questions.stem: A TCP syslog receiver reports framing errors despite valid fields. What layer first?

options.text: RFC 6587 record framing on the TCP stream
options.feedback: Correct. TCP has no message boundaries; framing must match the receiver.

options.text: FortiAnalyzer archive retention age
options.feedback: Not correct: Archive retention does not define TCP boundaries.

options.text: FortiGate forward policy ID
options.feedback: Not correct: Forward policy IDs are unrelated to syslog framing.

options.text: Receiver dashboard time zone only
options.feedback: Not correct: Time-zone display does not fix record splitting.

questions.stem: Which setting enables RFC 6587 octet-counting?

options.text: set fwd-syslog-format rfc-5424
options.feedback: Not correct: RFC 5424 selects content format, not framing.

options.text: set fwd-syslog-transparent enable
options.feedback: Correct. Transparent framing prefixes each record with its byte length.

options.text: set mode aggregation
options.feedback: Not correct: Aggregation is a scheduled FAZ-to-FAZ mode.

options.text: set log-forward-service accept-aggregation enable
options.feedback: Not correct: Aggregation acceptance does not change a syslog TCP stream.

questions.stem: What does fwd-syslog-format rfc-5424 change?

options.text: The TCP delimiter or byte count
options.feedback: Not correct: Framing is controlled separately by fwd-syslog-transparent.

options.text: The FortiAnalyzer disk quota
options.feedback: Not correct: Disk quota affects storage, not serialization.

options.text: The syslog message content format
options.feedback: Correct. The format setting changes message structure, not framing.

options.text: The daily aggregation start hour
options.feedback: Not correct: Aggregation time belongs to another mode.

questions.stem: Receiver expects octet-counting but sender uses delimiter framing. What symptom fits?

options.text: A FortiAP roaming-threshold alarm
options.feedback: Not correct: Roaming thresholds do not parse syslog streams.

options.text: A local-in policy denial on port1
options.feedback: Not correct: Local-in controls traffic destined to FortiGate.

options.text: A FortiSwitch leave-timer event
options.feedback: Not correct: VLAN pruning timers do not affect receiver framing.

options.text: Non-Transparent Framing errors or merged records
options.feedback: Correct. A framing mismatch can make the receiver reject or mis-segment TCP records.

questions.stem: What does dynamic VLAN pruning change on an ISL?

options.text: The VLAN set carried based on learned activity
options.feedback: Correct. Pruning narrows trunk carriage to VLANs indicated active downstream.

options.text: The VLAN database numbering scheme
options.feedback: Not correct: It does not renumber configured VLANs.

options.text: The switch DHCP address pool
options.feedback: Not correct: DHCP pool settings are a separate Layer 3 service.

options.text: The spanning-tree root priority
options.feedback: Not correct: STP root priority is not the pruning mechanism.

questions.stem: What is the documented default state of dynamic VLAN pruning?

options.text: Enabled automatically on every ISL
options.feedback: Not correct: It is not automatically enabled on every ISL.

options.text: Disabled until an administrator enables it
options.feedback: Correct. FortiSwitchOS 7.6.1 documents pruning as disabled by default.

options.text: Enabled only with storm control
options.feedback: Not correct: Storm control is unrelated.

options.text: Enabled by setting leave-timer to zero
options.feedback: Not correct: Zero is not the documented enable procedure.

questions.stem: What do join-timer and leave-timer control?

options.text: MAC aging and ARP cache expiration
options.feedback: Not correct: MAC/ARP timers manage different tables.

options.text: PoE allocation and guard band
options.feedback: Not correct: PoE settings manage power budgets.

options.text: Join advertisement interval and inactive-state delay
options.feedback: Correct. Join controls repeated Join messages; leave controls inactive-state delay.

options.text: STP hello interval and root election
options.feedback: Not correct: STP timers do not define GVRP pruning timers.

questions.stem: Which command lists VLANs learned by pruning on port10?

options.text: diagnose switch mac-address-table list port10
options.feedback: Not correct: A MAC table does not report pruning state.

options.text: get router info routing-table all port10
options.feedback: Not correct: The routing table is Layer 3 evidence.

options.text: diagnose switch poe status port10
options.feedback: Not correct: PoE status is unrelated to GVRP membership.

options.text: diagnose switch vlan-pruning dynamic-vlan list port10
options.feedback: Correct. The dynamic-vlan list displays the learned active set for an interface.

questions.stem: APs destabilize after upgrade and assigned legacy profile has lldp disable. Focused test?

options.text: Enable LLDP on one affected profile and observe
options.feedback: Correct. The older Fortinet scenario links legacy LLDP-disabled profiles with AP instability.

options.text: Increase every radio's transmit power immediately
options.feedback: Not correct: RF power is not the documented profile-state boundary.

options.text: Disable CAPWAP encryption across all APs
options.feedback: Not correct: Disabling encryption is risky and unrelated.

options.text: Change client roaming RSSI threshold first
options.feedback: Not correct: Roaming thresholds do not fix switch neighbor discovery.

questions.stem: Where should effective LLDP setting be verified first?

options.text: Only the global SSID name
options.feedback: Not correct: SSID naming does not show the profile flag.

options.text: The WTP profile actually assigned to the AP
options.feedback: Correct. The stored lldp value lives in the assigned WTP profile.

options.text: FortiAnalyzer archive retention setting
options.feedback: Not correct: Archive retention is unrelated.

options.text: The endpoint DHCP lease duration
options.feedback: Not correct: DHCP lease duration does not prove LLDP state.

questions.stem: What does a healthy AP ping prove when controller state still flaps?

options.text: That the WTP profile is definitely correct
options.feedback: Not correct: Reachability cannot validate the assigned profile.

options.text: That the radio has no interference
options.feedback: Not correct: Ping says nothing about RF interference.

options.text: IP reachability only, not completed WTP management
options.feedback: Correct. Ping does not prove profile, CAPWAP state, or neighbor learning.

options.text: That the switch accepted all LLDP data
options.feedback: Not correct: Switch LLDP state requires separate evidence.

questions.stem: Which evidence best distinguishes LLDP profile issue from RF roaming?

options.text: Only client RSSI from one handset
options.feedback: Not correct: RSSI is RF evidence, not wired neighbor state.

options.text: Only the DHCP server lease table
options.feedback: Not correct: DHCP leases do not prove LLDP.

options.text: Only a FortiGate forward-policy hit
options.feedback: Not correct: Transit policy hits are not AP profile evidence.

options.text: Profile lldp value plus switch neighbor state
options.feedback: Correct. Configuration and neighbor table directly test LLDP behavior.

questions.stem: FortiNAC sends Disconnect-Request but switch never acknowledges. First check?

options.text: Switch CoA listener, accounting access, and UDP 3799
options.feedback: Correct. Sending does not prove acceptance; listener and return path matter.

options.text: Only the user's browser cache
options.feedback: Not correct: Browser cache does not affect RADIUS control.

options.text: FortiAnalyzer report scheduling
options.feedback: Not correct: Report scheduling does not handle CoA.

options.text: The FortiAP radio channel plan
options.feedback: Not correct: Radio channel planning is unrelated.

questions.stem: Which FortiSwitch interface option is required to receive CoA?

options.text: allowaccess http only on user VLAN
options.feedback: Not correct: HTTP access alone does not permit RADIUS CoA.

options.text: allowaccess radius-acct on receiving interface
options.feedback: Correct. FortiSwitch documentation requires radius-acct on interfaces receiving CoA.

options.text: set vlan-pruning enable on trunk
options.feedback: Not correct: VLAN pruning is unrelated.

options.text: set poe-mode high on access port
options.feedback: Not correct: PoE mode does not affect UDP 3799.

questions.stem: How does Disconnect-Request differ from attribute-change CoA?

options.text: Both only update inventory labels
options.feedback: Not correct: Inventory labels do not define the RADIUS transaction.

options.text: Disconnect edits switch config directly
options.feedback: Not correct: The message does not directly rewrite switch config.

options.text: Disconnect flushes session; CoA changes attributes
options.feedback: Correct. RFC 5176 supports distinct attribute-change and disconnect behavior.

options.text: CoA always forces a switch reboot
options.feedback: Not correct: CoA does not inherently reboot the switch.

questions.stem: VLAN-change CoA works but host-deletion disconnect times out. Check?

options.text: Only FortiNAC display name and icon
options.feedback: Not correct: Display labels do not authenticate RADIUS.

options.text: Only endpoint DNS suffix
options.feedback: Not correct: DNS suffix is not the CoA return path.

options.text: Only switch spanning-tree root ID
options.feedback: Not correct: STP root ID does not explain a missing UDP response.

options.text: Source IP, shared secret, accounting and response path
options.feedback: Correct. Different transactions can expose listener, secret, routing, or support differences.

questions.stem: How does FortiNAC-F decide when to stop evaluating ranked profiling rules?

options.text: On pass, fail, or cannot-evaluate
options.feedback: Correct. Unavailable required data can stop evaluation instead of skipping a rule.

options.text: Every missing attribute is always skipped
options.feedback: Not correct: Missing data can yield cannot-evaluate.

options.text: Rules are evaluated randomly
options.feedback: Not correct: Rule order is configured, not random.

options.text: Only the final rule can classify
options.feedback: Not correct: Earlier rules can classify an endpoint.

questions.stem: What delivers DHCP fingerprint packets across routed VLANs?

options.text: A DHCP server running on eth0
options.feedback: Not correct: FortiNAC is not the endpoint DHCP server here.

options.text: An IP Helper pointing to management eth0
options.feedback: Correct. The guide recommends L3 IP Helper to the management listener.

options.text: A mirror sent to isolation interface
options.feedback: Not correct: The isolation interface is not the recommended profiling destination.

options.text: A longer DHCP lease on endpoints
options.feedback: Not correct: Lease duration does not deliver packets.

questions.stem: Why combine OUI, FortiGuard category, DHCP and behavior?

options.text: Each signal guarantees unique hardware identity
options.feedback: Not correct: OUI and DHCP can be ambiguous or absent.

options.text: Combining signals bypasses rule ranking
options.feedback: Not correct: Ranking still controls evaluation order.

options.text: Independent signals reduce single-fingerprint misclassification
options.feedback: Correct. Signals are complementary; no one signal is universally definitive.

options.text: Behavior removes the need for licensing
options.feedback: Not correct: FortiGuard-backed classification can depend on license/connectivity.

questions.stem: A static-IP PLC never matches DHCP fingerprint rule. Likely reason?

options.text: FortiGuard always blocks static addresses
options.feedback: Not correct: FortiGuard is not a blanket static-IP block.

options.text: MAC OUI cannot be read on Ethernet
options.feedback: Not correct: OUI comes from the MAC address.

options.text: Every device needs an 802.1X supplicant
options.feedback: Not correct: Profiling has methods for non-802.1X devices.

options.text: It sends no DHCP fingerprint packets
options.feedback: Correct. Static-IP endpoints may never send DHCP Discover/Request/Inform.

questions.stem: What is the difference between global pre-filter and per-FortiGate filter?

options.text: Pre-filter controls ingestion; device filter controls export
options.feedback: Correct. Global pre-filter is upstream of FAC database; device filter is downstream.

options.text: Both only alter firewall policy order
options.feedback: Not correct: Neither edits firewall rule order.

options.text: Pre-filter runs after every FortiGate receives sessions
options.feedback: Not correct: Pre-filter is not a post-export filter.

options.text: Device filter changes LDAP passwords
options.feedback: Not correct: FSSO filtering does not change LDAP credentials.

questions.stem: Which filter scope includes groups under an organizational unit?

options.text: A single user DN only
options.feedback: Not correct: A user DN selects one user.

options.text: A group-container DN with subcontainer scope
options.feedback: Correct. Group-container scope includes groups beneath the selected LDAP container.

options.text: An IP object without LDAP scope
options.feedback: Not correct: IP objects do not define LDAP group scope.

options.text: A firewall subnet address group
options.feedback: Not correct: Firewall address groups are unrelated to LDAP objects.

questions.stem: User appears in FAC SSO Sessions but not one FortiGate. Inspect?

options.text: The global pre-filter first in every case
options.feedback: Not correct: Global changes could affect every consumer unnecessarily.

options.text: The AP LLDP neighbor table
options.feedback: Not correct: LLDP is unrelated.

options.text: That FortiGate's named export filter and connector
options.feedback: Correct. Presence in FAC suggests ingestion succeeded; per-device export may exclude it.

options.text: FortiPAM application filter
options.feedback: Not correct: FortiPAM controls Windows execution.

questions.stem: Why create separate FSSO filters for different FortiGates?

options.text: It forces all users into global database
options.feedback: Not correct: Global ingestion is a separate stage.

options.text: It replaces LDAP polling with SNMP traps
options.feedback: Not correct: SNMP traps do not replace FSSO login collection.

options.text: It grants all selected users admin access
options.feedback: Not correct: FSSO visibility does not grant administrator privileges.

options.text: Each firewall receives its intended group subset
options.feedback: Correct. Per-device filters allow distinct export scope from one FAC database.

questions.stem: What is the control-channel prerequisite for Windows Application Filter?

options.text: WinRM on Windows target plus privileged account
options.feedback: Correct. FortiPAM manages target-side application rules through WinRM.

options.text: A forward policy with deep inspection
options.feedback: Not correct: Security profiles are not the deployment control plane.

options.text: An AP profile with LLDP enabled
options.feedback: Not correct: Wireless settings are unrelated.

options.text: A FortiAnalyzer aggregation schedule
options.feedback: Not correct: Log aggregation is unrelated to Windows policy.

questions.stem: Why can a saved filter profile have no target effect?

options.text: FortiPAM dashboard uses a dark theme
options.feedback: Not correct: Dashboard appearance does not control enforcement.

options.text: It was not attached to the tested secret
options.feedback: Correct. The profile is applied through a secret; an unattached profile does not enforce.

options.text: Windows host has static IP
options.feedback: Not correct: Static IP does not inherently prevent filtering.

options.text: FortiAnalyzer has no archive quota
options.feedback: Not correct: Archive quota is unrelated.

questions.stem: What does the target's Windows Application Filter tab verify?

options.text: Which local-in rule matched traffic
options.feedback: Not correct: Local-in logs belong to FortiGate.

options.text: Which VLANs GVRP pruned
options.feedback: Not correct: VLAN pruning is a switch function.

options.text: Which accounts have which filters applied
options.feedback: Correct. The target view shows accounts and applied filter profiles.

options.text: Which FSSO users were exported
options.feedback: Not correct: FSSO export is managed by FortiAuthenticator.

questions.stem: Which diagnostic approach fits a secret launch/filter failure?

options.text: Change every target password before capture
options.feedback: Not correct: Password rotation is separate and may worsen the incident.

options.text: Disable WinRM and retry
options.feedback: Not correct: WinRM is a prerequisite, not a first disable.

options.text: Increase all firewall session TTL values
options.feedback: Not correct: Session TTL is not the filter diagnostic.

options.text: Enable focused secret and HTTP WAD debug
options.feedback: Correct. Focused secret/HTTP verbose diagnostics expose the launch control transaction.

questions.stem: What does successful ping prove about WMI/OMI monitoring?

options.text: IP reachability, not WinRM authorization or query success
options.feedback: Correct. WMI/OMI needs service, credentials, permissions, and query success.

options.text: Every Windows Event ID is collected
options.feedback: Not correct: Event collection depends on source/template and audit settings.

options.text: Remediation permissions are sufficient
options.feedback: Not correct: Remediation can require additional WinRM setup.

options.text: Windows Agent template is associated
options.feedback: Not correct: Agent association is a separate collection path.

questions.stem: Which sequence describes Windows Agent log collection?

options.text: Enable WMI only and skip template
options.feedback: Not correct: Agent collection requires template configuration.

options.text: Install agent, define template, associate agent, verify events
options.feedback: Correct. The Supervisor distributes monitoring policy after template association.

options.text: Create FortiGate policy then import to CMDB
options.feedback: Not correct: Firewall policies are not monitor templates.

options.text: Add event IDs to VLAN pruning
options.feedback: Not correct: Event IDs are not pruning criteria.

questions.stem: How are Windows Agent event IDs entered in a template?

options.text: One CIDR subnet per event type
options.feedback: Not correct: CIDR is IP-network notation.

options.text: A comma-separated list of switch ports
options.feedback: Not correct: Switch ports are unrelated.

options.text: Include/exclude IDs as semicolon-separated lists
options.feedback: Correct. The guide describes semicolon-separated IDs for inclusion and exclusion.

options.text: Only the Windows host name
options.feedback: Not correct: Hostname identifies an agent but does not select events.

questions.stem: Agent is connected but Security events are absent. Next check?

options.text: Change FortiGate local-in order
options.feedback: Not correct: Local-in order does not configure Windows collection.

options.text: Increase FortiSwitch leave-timer
options.feedback: Not correct: Pruning timers do not select Windows events.

options.text: Change FortiSASE exemptions
options.feedback: Not correct: SSL exemptions do not affect agent event IDs.

options.text: Template association, event filters, and Windows audit source
options.feedback: Correct. Agent status does not prove the desired event is enabled or generated.

questions.stem: Which mode can inspect encrypted payloads for DLP or file filtering?

options.text: Deep inspection with a trusted inspection CA
options.feedback: Correct. Deep inspection decrypts content for payload-aware profiles and re-encrypts upstream.

options.text: Certificate inspection without decryption
options.feedback: Not correct: Certificate inspection sees TLS metadata, not payload.

options.text: No inspection with URL metadata only
options.feedback: Not correct: No inspection cannot provide decrypted content.

options.text: DNS filtering before TLS
options.feedback: Not correct: DNS filtering cannot inspect file bodies.

questions.stem: Why must endpoints trust the inspection CA?

options.text: It enables DHCP fingerprinting at switch
options.feedback: Not correct: DHCP fingerprinting is a NAC feature.

options.text: Client sees an inspection certificate during interception
options.feedback: Correct. Deep inspection substitutes an inspection certificate on the client side.

options.text: It selects FortiGate local-in rule
options.feedback: Not correct: Local-in rules govern FortiGate-destined traffic.

options.text: It changes FortiManager template order
options.feedback: Not correct: Template ordering is unrelated to TLS trust.

questions.stem: HTTPS category filtering works but DLP does not inspect uploads. Why?

options.text: URL is always absent from DNS cache
options.feedback: Not correct: DNS cache does not show payload decryption.

options.text: Switch pruning removed the DLP VLAN
options.feedback: Not correct: VLAN pruning does not define SASE inspection mode.

options.text: Flow is certificate-only or exempt from deep inspection
options.feedback: Correct. Metadata inspection can categorize URLs but cannot read encrypted upload content.

options.text: FortiSIEM agent lacks a template
options.feedback: Not correct: Windows Agent templates do not configure SASE DLP.

questions.stem: One SaaS destination bypasses payload inspection. What should be reviewed?

options.text: FortiGate DHCP lease time
options.feedback: Not correct: DHCP leases do not determine SASE exemptions.

options.text: FortiPAM privileged account name
options.feedback: Not correct: PAM account identity is unrelated.

options.text: FortiSwitch GVRP counters
options.feedback: Not correct: GVRP counters do not affect SaaS inspection.

options.text: Host/category exemptions and assigned profile group
options.feedback: Correct. A deep-inspection exemption or different policy assignment can bypass decryption.

questions.stem: Which traffic is local-out?

options.text: Traffic generated by FortiGate services to external peers
options.feedback: Correct. Local-out is self-originating traffic such as DNS, FortiGuard, syslog, and authentication.

options.text: Client traffic forwarded between interfaces
options.feedback: Not correct: Forwarded client traffic uses the transit path.

options.text: Only packets denied by forward policy
options.feedback: Not correct: A deny action does not define local-out.

options.text: Only RADIUS Access-Accept replies
options.feedback: Not correct: RADIUS replies are not the definition of all local-out traffic.

questions.stem: Which setting asks system DNS to use SD-WAN egress selection?

options.text: set local-in-policy-log enable
options.feedback: Not correct: Local-in logging controls traffic records.

options.text: set interface-select-method sdwan
options.feedback: Correct. System DNS supports a local-out method that can use SD-WAN.

options.text: set fwd-syslog-transparent enable
options.feedback: Not correct: Syslog framing controls serialization.

options.text: set vlan-pruning enable
options.feedback: Not correct: VLAN pruning is a switch Layer 2 feature.

questions.stem: Why might an existing FortiManager tunnel not move after SLA change?

options.text: Every local-out session resets on every SLA change
options.feedback: Not correct: Existing sessions are not automatically torn down for every SLA change.

options.text: FortiManager tunnel is ordinary transit policy traffic
options.feedback: Not correct: The tunnel is a FortiGate-originated control session.

options.text: Local-out SD-WAN choice is checked at session creation
options.feedback: Correct. Central-management traffic is not terminated just because SD-WAN logic changes.

options.text: FortiSwitch leave timer holds the tunnel open
options.feedback: Not correct: VLAN pruning timers do not govern the tunnel.

questions.stem: When manually specifying local-out egress, what else needs review?

options.text: FortiNAC profiling rule rank
options.feedback: Not correct: NAC rule rank does not select FortiGate source IP.

options.text: FortiPAM filter exception
options.feedback: Not correct: PAM exceptions are unrelated.

options.text: FortiAP roaming RSSI threshold
options.feedback: Not correct: RSSI controls wireless handoff.

options.text: Actual egress interface and chosen source IP
options.feedback: Correct. A manual source may need to match upstream routing and allowlists.

questions.stem: A local traffic log shows policyid=0. What should you avoid assuming?

options.text: That it means forward-policy implicit deny
options.feedback: Correct. Built-in local-in policies can log policyid=0; context differs from forward logs.

options.text: That the packet was an allowed transit flow
options.feedback: Not correct: Local traffic is not necessarily transit.

options.text: That IPv6 local-in was automatically matched
options.feedback: Not correct: IPv4 and IPv6 tables are separate.

options.text: That an SSL profile inspected payload
options.feedback: Not correct: A policy ID alone does not prove decryption.

questions.stem: Which pair separates syslog payload format from TCP framing?

options.text: Both select daily aggregation hour
options.feedback: Not correct: Aggregation time and retention are separate controls.

options.text: fwd-syslog-format selects content; transparent selects framing
options.feedback: Correct. FortiAnalyzer treats message format and stream framing independently.

options.text: Transparent selects RFC5424 fields; format selects byte count
options.feedback: Not correct: The options have the opposite responsibilities stated.

options.text: Both enable disk retention
options.feedback: Not correct: Neither setting enables disk retention.
